title: Adaptive embedding model lifecycle: staggered rollforward, soft deprecations, and tenant-specific quality fences
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and implement a staged 'rollforward' process to onboard new embedding models (including quantized variants) into the reranking + vector-search stack with minimal tenant disruption. The goal is higher-quality embeddings in the catalog while preserving latency SLOs and providing automated soft-deprecation for legacy models. This ticket focuses on policy, rollout mechanics, telemetry gating, and an operational remediation path that ties into the reranking endpoint fallback.

Background: We have frequent new embedding candidates (open checkpoints, quantized builds) that show improved retrieval quality on aggregate but cause per-tenant regressions due to data skew (domain-specific tokens, custom length distributions). Current onboarding is either full-cutover or simple canaries; both are brittle at scale. We need a system that can: (1) surface per-tenant quality deltas, (2) automatically limit exposure to affected tenants, (3) gracefully sunset deprecated variants, and (4) ensure reranker and downstream pipelines remain stable and performant.

Scope and goals:
- Implement a staged rollforward orchestration (shadow -> mixed -> percent-split -> default) that supports per-tenant fences (KL/quality/cosine-drift thresholds).
- Add an embedding compatibility probe ("embed-aligner") that computes cross-model similarity alignment (orthogonal Procrustes + small linear mapping) to help map similarity distributions between model variants.
- Integrate quality fences based on a small set of signal families: paired-prompt A/B semantics (regression deltas), average cosine shift distributions, and downstream reranking NDCG deltas on tenant-specific probe sets.
- Wire fallback behavior in the reranking endpoint: when a tenant crosses a degradation fence, route their traffic to a stable legacy variant or to reranker-only hybrid (queries use legacy embeddings + new reranker) per policy.
- Ensure rollout is latency-safe: maintain per-model batching profiles, KV cache warmup policies, and quantized kernel compatibility checks so new models don’t cause tail-latency spikes.

Design notes:
- Rollforward states: SHADOW (no production traffic, full telemetry), MIXED (sticky-tenant mixed buckets, 5-20% sample), SPLIT (global percentage routing), DEFAULT (full swap). Each stage promotes by monitoring a set of pass/fail gates.
- Quality gates: KL divergence of embedding distributions per-tenant (threshold configurable), pairwise recall/NDCG delta on tenant probe sets (e.g., regress if > 3% drop), and tail-latency uplift (> 10% p95 increase triggers fail).
- Alignment tooling: embed-aligner produces a small mapping artifact saved in model metadata to allow quick offline normalization; used by A/B eval harness to reduce false positives from dimension subspace rotations.
- Telemetry: new metrics (embed_kl_delta, embed_cosine_shift_p95, rerank_ndcg_delta, embed_kv_cache_warmup_hit_rate) and dashboards in Datadog linked in Links.
- Operator flows: manual pause/resume in Console rollouts, automated tenant quarantine with email/Slack alert and rollback playbook, and an on-call runbook for investigating fences.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria list below)

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives from distribution metrics: mitigate via embed-aligner normalization + aggregated probe sets.
- Latency regressions from quantized variants: require kernel compatibility tests in CI and staged warmup with KV priming traffic.
- Tenant confusion: Console UX must show per-tenant rollforward status and allow manual override.

Implementation approach:
1) Build embed-aligner service (offline job) + model metadata extension to publish alignment artifact.
2) Extend canary/rollout controller with per-tenant routing and stages above.
3) Add telemetry and alarms; create default probe-sets for top 200 tenants and a mechanism for tenant owners to upload/customize.
4) Integrate reranking endpoint fallback logic and implement hybrid reranker-only path.
5) Smoke test on staging with a small set of internal tenants; run 2-week shadow evaluation.

Notes on compatibility: document requirements for new models (embedding dimension parity preferred; if not, map via embed-aligner; require same tokenizer or provide tokenizer mapping). Quantized builds must expose a declared kernel profile.

Operationally relevant artifacts: design spec -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Adaptive+Embedding+Rollforward; embed-aligner prototype -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/embed-aligner/pull/47; rollout controller changes -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/213; datadog dashboard -> https://app.datadog.com/dashboard/redwood/embed-rollforward-overview
acceptance_criteria: embed-aligner produces an alignment artifact for a candidate model and the artifact is stored in model metadata
Rollout controller supports SHADOW, MIXED, SPLIT, DEFAULT states and per-tenant routing rules
Quality gates implemented: embed_kl_delta, embed_cosine_shift_p95, rerank_ndcg_delta, latency_p95_uplift
Reranking endpoint supports automatic fallback to legacy embedding variant or hybrid reranker-only path when tenant fence trips
Datadog dashboards and alerts created; alert runbook links present in Console
Staging shadow evaluation shows no tenant-level NDCG regression > 2% for top 80% traffic within 14 days
Latency SLOs maintained (no >10% p95 uplift) during MIXED and SPLIT phases in canary runs
